issue: PDF URL redirect handling causes a document to fail before threat scanning. When external medical research journals or PubMed links issue a 301/302 redirect header, pdfFetcher terminates the stream early with ERR_UNHANDLED_REDIRECT instead of resolving the final target URI, causing threatScanner to receive a 0-byte buffer.

evidence.provenance: Stack trace frames + AST import analysis + failing unit test trace

supporting: Failing execution trace enters fetchPdfStream before crash at line 42
HTTP 302 redirect response branch exists in this file with missing recursive follow logic
Failing integration test imports this module and mocks a redirect response
contradictory: documentLoader.ts also inspects Content-Type headers before delegating

supporting: Receives zero-byte buffer error when redirect occurs
contradictory: Unit tests for scanBufferPayload with valid buffers pass with 100% success
Scanner is never called when redirect throws upfront in fetcher

hypotheses.title: Redirect handling in fetchPdfStream drops response stream
PDF Content-Type validation rejects redirected intermediate HTML header
ThreatScanner timeout rejects slow redirect resolution

patch_proposed.invariant: Redirected PDF URLs must resolve to the final PDF resource without bypassing threat scanning.
